Halting of trains at Alam Nagar
station
†*261. SHRI BANWARI LAL
KANCHHAL: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether he is aware of demonstration
under the leadership of Uttar Pradesh Jan
Kalyan Samiti for halting of various trains
at Alam Nagar railway station in Lucknow;
(b) whether his Ministry is considering
the 21-point demand letter submitted by them;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government would
consider halt of various trains at Alam Nagar
station in public interest; and
(e) if so, by when and if not, the reason
therefor?
TPDS beneficiaries in Andhra
Pradesh
*262. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) the details of beneficiaries under
TPDS under APL, BPL and AAY in the
State of Andhra Pradesh during the last five
years, year-wise and district-wise;
(b) the number of Fair Price Shops that
are distributing foodgrains in the State to
those beneficiaries;
(c) whether it is a fact that Government
monitors PDS on monthly-basis;
(d) if so, the details of mechanism under
which Government monitors PDS on
monthly-basis;
(e) whether the States are mandated to
submit form-'C' as required under PDS
Order, 2001; and
(f) if so, the details thereof with regard
to Andhra Pradesh?
Expansion of Crop Insurance Policy
*263. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARAT:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
formulated any proposal to expand the
Crop Insurance Policy as per the
recommendation of Dr. M.S. Swaminathan
Committee; and
(b) whether women are being included
in the farm insurance scheme?

Upgradation of medical institutions
under PMSSY
*264. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) what steps have been taken for the
upgradation of 13 Medical institutions under
the PMSSY and the details regarding
individual institutions;
(b) by when such upgradation is likely to
be completed; and
(c) by when the new medical institution
being created under this scheme at Jodhpur
would be completed?
Adverse impact of healthcare tourism
*265. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have as a
policy,  acquiesced with many States
promoting healthcare tourism causing a
drain on scarce medicare resources both in
infrastructure and doctors/paramedics
badly needed to provide basic healthcare
to the locals; and
(b) whether private investment in health
sector attempts to provide medicare to rich
and elite including foreign tourists which
would deprive the right of the poor Indians
for basic medicare at affordable costs?
Committee on AIIMS
*266. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether four-member committee
constituted by the Centre to study the
functioning of the AIIMS has submitted its
report to Government;
(b) if so, what are the main
recommendations made by the Committee;
(c) whether with an aim of reducing
patient load in its main hospital AIIMS,
Government are considering setting up of
ten new super--specialities, self-sufficient
centers like AIIMS in the country;
(d) what are the places where these
centers are likely to be set up; and
(e) by when these centers would start
functioning?
Petroleum, Chemicals and Petro-
chemical Investment Regions
*267. SHRIMATI S.G. INDIRA:
SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had decided to set up massive petroleum,
chemical and petro-chemical investment
regions across the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government had shortlisted five best
locations in this regard; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Maternal Healthcare Scheme
*268. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a new free
Maternal Healthcare Scheme has been launched
to benefit women living below poverty line in
need of pre-pregnancy care, institutional
deliveries, post-natal care, etc.; and
(b) if so, the salient features of the
scheme and the places where it has been
implemented?

Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
*269. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Food
Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has still
not come into force;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government have studied
likely repercussions of this Act, on small
and marginal traders;
(d) if so, the details thereof;
(e) by when the rules under this Act are
likely to be framed by Government;
(f) whether it is also a fact that
Government have still not decided about
the administrative Ministry which would
implement the provisions of this Act; and
(g) if so, the details thereof?
Multi Speciality Veterinary Centre
and Research Institute in Kerala
*270. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the Minister for Food, Civil
Supplies and Animal Husbandry in Kerala
has forwarded a proposal for setting up of a
Multi Speciality Veterinary Centre and
Research Institute in Kerala;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the decision of the Central
Government on this proposal?
Increasing MSP of wheat and bonus
thereon
†*271. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
  SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the Minimum Support Price of
wheat in the last year and amount of bonus
given to the farmers per quintal;
(b) the rate at which private companies
purchased wheat from the farmers and the
shortage in procurement of wheat by
Government as compared to the target;
(c) whether Government would increase
the Minimum Support Price of wheat and
increase the bonus, keeping in view the
pathetic condition of farmers, continuous
increase in production cost and the incidents
of suicides being committed by farmers; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Security of railway passengers
*272. DR. P.C. ALEXANDER: Will the
Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) the respective responsibilities of the
State Police and the Railway Police for the
security of the persons and properties of
railway passengers;
(b) further measures which Government
propose to take to ensure more effective
security for railway passengers; and
(c) the measures proposed to be taken
to ensure proper co-ordination between the
police departments of the Railways and
the State Governments and to enforce
accountability of those responsible for the
security of the railway passengers?
Improving agriculture
*273. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has called for
enhancing the outlays for agriculture in the

86
Eleventh Five Year Plan, so that, State
Governments are provided adequate funds,
Strengthen infrastructure and help capital
formation and investment in agriculture;
(b) if so, whether State Agriculture
Ministers' conference was held on 22nd

recommendations of the National
Commission on Farmers which submitted
its final report to Government in October,

Prices of pulses
*274. SHRI SURESH BHARDWAJ:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
cognizance of rise in prices of pulses during
the recent months;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
details of movement of prices of pulses
during the current year and the comparative
prices of pulses during the last three years;
(c) the reasons for price rise; and
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to assuage the prices of
pulses?
Survey on health, nutrition and behaviour
*275. SHRI JANARDHANA
POOJARY: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether National Family Health
survey was conducted to gather information
on health, nutrition and behaviour;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that the findings
of the survey indicates that the indices on
health and development are not encouraging;
(d) if so, the details thereof, with the
details of funds generated from various
sources, allocated and spent during the last
five years on health particularly in respect
of women and children in rural areas, year-
wise and State-wise; and
(e) what measures Government propose
to initiate to improve the situation and the
time-frame, if any, set for the purpose?
Institutional deliveries
*276. SHRI KANJIBHAI PATEL: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number
of institutional deliveries in the country has
reached 50 per cent mark;
(b) if so, the reasons for non-coverage
of the remaining 50 per cent; and
(c) the measures being taken to raise the
percentage of such deliveries?

regarding introducing trains with speed up
to 250 km. per hour is under his active
consideration;

stock and the track is capable of
withstanding movement of such high-speed

Shrinking of wetlands
†*278. SHRI JANESHWAR MISHRA:
SHRI BRIJ BHUSHAN
TIWARI:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
wetlands such as lakes, ponds and wet areas
in the country especially in the metro cities
are shrinking rapidly;
(b) if so, whether Government have
formulated any specific action plan to control

Closing of halt stations
†*279. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be pleased
to state:
(a) the total number of halt stations in
the country alongwith details thereof; State-
wise;
(b) to what extent the Ministry is
earning profit from these halt stations; and
(c) whether there is any scheme in offing
to close those halt stations which are
running in loss?
Non-availability of treatments to
AIDS patients
*280. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India has a
large number of HIV/AIDS patients, but
only 7% of those who need treatment are
getting it, as per UNAIDS report 2006;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) what is the action plan of
Government to augment health
infrastructure and devise other measures
to control this rising trend; and
(d) what is the status of this menace in
Orissa and how far the Centre has helped
both physically and financially to control
this menace in the backward State?
